verdicts.evidence: Circulate as students discuss. Observe students sharing information about their selected pattern in the sky, using sentence frames to add on to the discussion, and using their notes as a resource as they share and discuss.
verdicts.rationale: The standard requires students to share relevant and accurate information through a variety of different modes (C). During the Science Talk protocol, students share information about observable sky patterns orally, using their notes sheets to ensure accuracy: "Observe students sharing information about their selected pattern in the sky, using sentence frames to add on to the discussion, and using their notes as a resource as they share and discuss." Teacher feedback confirms the accuracy expectation: "I saw many of you consult your notes sheet during your discussions to make sure you were sharing accurate information with your classmates." The relevance and accuracy clauses are met. The variety-of-modes clause is only partially met: students communicate orally (Science Talk) and produce written/drawn Sky Notebook entries, but the Notebook task is framed as observation-recording rather than sharing information with an audience through a distinct communicative mode, making the "variety of different modes" component thin.
